decisions.reason: As a newly launched feature that fits the firm's identity-and-secure-services platform, it is likely to be retained while management gives this complementary offer more time unless early adoption clearly misses aspiration levels.

An identity-linked payment wallet is close to the firm's core super-app and secure-ecosystem logic, so an established firm with some slack would usually keep it unless overlap or weak customer uptake becomes obvious.

This authenticator is strategically relevant but more niche and less central to the firm's platform direction, so it faces the highest review risk if results disappoint, though not enough to make dropping the most likely outcome yet.
A secure payment and wallet framework matches the firm's core capabilities and having its own page signals commitment, which makes retention more likely than withdrawal in the next year.

Because this product is presented as the flagship expression of the firm's future direction, management is very unlikely to remove it after only a short market test even if initial results are still uncertain.

The application-shielding library draws directly on the firm's long-standing security expertise and dedicated market presentation, so it is likely to stay unless commercial traction falls well below aspiration.
